dedupe_keys.name: latin america digital infrastructure comparative observatory

description: This comparative observatory assembles digital-infrastructure indicators for eight Latin American markets. Sebastian Elgueta Godoy publishes a 27-variable country benchmark and separate tables for cloud regions, exchanges, selected submarine systems and operator presence. Coverage includes Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Mexico, Panama and Peru. Version 0.2.0 was released in September 2026, with a frozen evidence cutoff of 13 August. The source ledger provides metric-level lineage and selected detailed tables retain row-level source references. Public CSV resources and an archived release are free to access. MIT covers software and documentation; third-party observations retain their original terms. A limitation is that the benchmark has no separate source URL in every cell. Several measures also require careful interpretation: grid-connection days use a 2019-era historical proxy, electricity tariffs are business prices, and physical-distance latency estimates are not measured network latency. Operational and announced infrastructure remain separate. Simulation uses include comparative siting, energy-demand and connectivity scenarios. It relates to data-peeringdb and data-telegeography-submarine-cable-map as broader infrastructure reference sources. The observatory is not a facility-level census, and neither its data rows nor its numerical comparisons were reproduced.
licence: MIT applies to software and documentation only; source-derived observations retain original publisher terms
